commentary.text: I’m establishing an immediate central foothold with Red, beginning a coordinated Red–Yellow attempt to control the four winning squares.

I’m taking the lower central square with Blue, creating a vertical clamp on the advanced Red at (3,3). If it stays, another Blue can land at (2,3) and sandwich it against this piece; otherwise Red must surrender the center.
I’m taking a second central square and preparing Red to occupy (3,4), building immediate center pressure while keeping Yellow safe from any current sandwich.

I’m blocking Yellow’s immediate `7,2→4,2` sandwich against the central Blue piece. Green advances to (5,2), preserving Blue’s planned vertical capture of Red at (3,3) while developing toward the center.
I’m taking the third central square, tightening the center threat and pinning Blue’s piece at (4,3): if it leaves, Yellow can complete the center occupation.

I’m completing the prepared vertical clamp: Blue lands at (2,3), sandwiching and capturing Red at (3,3) against the Blue piece at (4,3). This breaks Red’s central pair and gives Blue a strong route toward occupying (3,3).
I advance Yellow behind Green’s piece on (5,2), pinning it in place: if it moves away, Yellow can reach (4,2) and sandwich Blue’s central piece against Yellow on (4,4).

Green advances to (3,2) while keeping the blocker at (5,2), so Yellow still cannot reach (4,2) to sandwich the central Blue. This also closes Red’s direct route from (0,2) to (3,2) and strengthens our approach to (3,3).
I’m staging a second Red beside the center. This supports a controlled shift into (3,3), followed by refilling (3,4), without exposing either piece to an immediate sandwich.

I’m occupying (3,3) with Blue and setting a concrete elimination threat: if the Red pair remains on row 3, Blue can shift from (3,7) to (3,6), sandwich both Reds against this new anchor and eliminate Red.

I’m occupying (3,6) to block Blue’s threatened move there, which would otherwise sandwich both Red pieces on (3,5) and (3,4) against Blue’s center piece. This preserves Red’s position and frees its next turn for a counterattack.

I’m lifting Green to (2,2) to preserve Blue’s center anchor while denying both Red sandwich tactics: (0,1)→(3,1) no longer finds a line, and the Green blocker on column 2 prevents (0,2)→(3,2). Green remains poised to return toward the center.
I’m developing the edge Red onto row 3, creating sandwich pressure on the Blue center piece at (3,3) using the Red piece at (3,4) as the far flank.

I’m advancing Blue to (4,7), threatening to slide to (4,5) and sandwich Yellow’s central piece at (4,4) against our Blue anchor at (4,3). If Yellow retreats, Blue can occupy (4,4); Green’s next priority remains (2,2)→(3,2) to block Red’s sandwich threat against (3,3).

I’m blocking Blue’s immediate route to (4,5), which would sandwich and capture our Yellow center piece. This also keeps all four central-square plans alive while giving Red time to challenge Blue’s center anchor.

I’m placing Green at (3,0) while leaving (2,2) in place to block Red’s route toward our center anchor. This prepares (2,2)→(3,2), which will sandwich the exposed Red at (3,1); meanwhile Red must answer Blue’s separate row-three capture threat.
I’m exploiting the Red flank already established on row 3: shifting into (3,2) sandwiches the Blue piece at (3,3) against Red at (3,4), removing a central defender.

Blue develops onto the open third file, guaranteeing access to (3,3). If Red occupies that center first, Blue can instead land at (2,3) and capture it against the Blue anchor at (4,3); otherwise Blue takes the center directly and prepares a clamp on Red’s row-three pair.

Green closes the vertical clamp at (4,2), capturing Red at (3,2) against the Green anchor at (2,2). Red now has two losses and must also dismantle Blue’s row-three sandwich threat from (3,7) to (3,6), leaving its central formation under severe pressure.
I’m repositioning Red between the two Green pieces while preserving the Yellow sandwich threat along row 4. This also prepares a Red recapture if Blue occupies (3,3).

Blue redeploys to (6,5), threatening to rise to (4,5) and sandwich Yellow’s center piece at (4,4) against our Blue anchor at (4,3). Yellow must now abandon or materially alter its central formation; if (4,4) is vacated, Blue can occupy it and advance our center-control plan.
This move exploits the Yellow anchor on (4,4): landing at (4,1) sandwiches the mixed Green–Blue line on (4,2) and (4,3), scoring two captures and clearing a central square.

Green shifts to (2,4), preparing to occupy the central square (3,4) while freeing Blue’s route to (3,3). Red now faces a fork: contest Green’s center entry or block Blue’s planned (6,5)→(4,5), which would capture Yellow at (4,6) against Blue’s anchor at (4,7).
I’m occupying the upper-right center while preserving the Red piece at (3,2). This creates a strong center-completion threat and makes any Blue block on (3,3) sit between two Red pieces.
Blue strikes at (4,5), sandwiching Yellow at (4,6) against the Blue piece on (4,7). This gains a clean capture while placing Blue beside the center, with (4,4) as the next pressure point.
I occupy a third central square, creating an immediate center-victory threat: Red can fill (3,3) next turn, and Green cannot reach or disrupt the center in time.

Green cannot currently reach (3,3) or dislodge a central piece, so I move the advanced Green onto the third file, preserving mobility and a route into the center if Red fails to complete its occupation.
The center is one square from complete Team A occupation. Red slides into (3,3), joining Red at (3,4) and Yellow at (4,3) and (4,4) for an immediate center victory.
